purpose: §10 detail: how the 7-way shared worktree/shared-Postgres pattern specifically produced this outcome.
observedPattern: This is the THIRD distinct manifestation of the same underlying shared-worktree/shared-Postgres hazard visible across this session and its own immediately-prior phase: (1) prior phases' agents reported sibling `git reset --hard` invocations wiping each other's uncommitted git work (recovered each time by the affected agent itself); (2) this phase's own Part A discovered a full Company-table wipe (this artifact's subject); (3) the same sharing pattern is why FWRG's own compiler run state ended up mixing two incompatible generations (05-half-written-state.json) once this incident-response's OWN two sequential attempts ran against the one shared instance.
structuralCause: Git worktrees correctly isolate each dispatched agent's CODE (each worktree is its own checkout, its own branch, its own working directory - this part of the harness's isolation model works exactly as intended). They do nothing to isolate STATE external to the git repository - and this project's Postgres database is exactly that: one physical server, one database, one schema, referenced identically from every worktree's own `.env`. Code isolation without data isolation is sufficient for the 6+ prior data-loss-shaped incidents this project's own history describes, and sufficient again here.
recommendation: Per-worktree (or per-parallel-test-run) database isolation is not an optional hardening step for this project - it is the direct, targeted fix for a hazard that has now caused real, repeated, unrecoverable-in-exact-form data loss (per this session's own prior finding that some 2026-08-25 LegalReviewRecord chronology is permanently unrecoverable in exact form). See 11-test-isolation-design.json for the design and 12+ for the implementation.
